chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Faddal, from Abu Ishaq Tha'labah ibn Maymun, from a man whose name he mentioned, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

"The most truthful of names is that which is named with servitude [to God], and the best of them are the names of the prophets. Indeed, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever is blessed with four children and does not name one of them with my name, has alienated me.'

key_terms.جَفَانِي: Has alienated me / turned away from me

ai.seo_question: What is the best name to give a child according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes a hierarchy of naming, prioritizing names that reflect *'ubudiyyah* (servitude to God) and the Prophet's own name, citing a specific criterion for familial connection. The Prophet’s statement regarding the four children highlights the importance of maintaining spiritual lineage and identity within the family unit, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding personal status. This narration underscores the theological weight of names as identifiers of faith and devotion, linking individual identity to the broader prophetic tradition.
